newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: No need for German rate cut now -- Buba's Welteke.
newsitem.headline: No need for German rate cut now -- Buba's Welteke.

text.p: There is no need at the moment for a reduction in German interest rates, Ernst Welteke, a member of the Bundesbank's decision-making council, said on Friday.
"At the current moment, there is no need for a reduction in interest rates," Welteke told Reuters Financial Television in an interview in Singapore.
Welteke also said Germany would not accept a softening of the criteria of the Maastricht Treaty.

Asked whether Germany would accept a softening, he said: "No, no. Not a softening," adding that three strict criteria -- those for inflation, interest rates, and exchange rates -- were important for European monetary union.
Welteke said the Bundesbank was looking at money supply and that M3 was above its target at the moment.
He added that the Bundesbank had room for manoeuvre as far as the open market interest rate was concerned because the discount rate was at 2.5 percent and the open market rate at three percent.
But he said there was no need at the moment for a cut in interest rates.
Welteke said that if there were to be a change in interest rates, it would be in the repo rate and not in the discount or Lombard rates.
When asked about exchange rates, Welteke said it was good to have a strong dollar.

"For our exporters in Germany and our weak economic situation in Germany, it's good to have a strong dollar. Therefore I think it's right that the G7 is interested in a strong dollar," he said, noting that the United States was interested in a strong dollar as well.
Asked about the recent strengthening of the mark against the yen, Welteke said that a strong yen against the mark would be helpful for European exporters.
"We are competing with lots of Japanese industries, therefore a strong yen would be helpful," Welteke said.
